newsitem.title: MEXICO: Female bullfighter draws capacity crowd in Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Female bullfighter draws capacity crowd in Mexico.

text.p: Spain's first female matador, Cristina Sanchez, drew a capacity crowd for her debut appearance at the Mexico City bullring on Sunday, but local veteran Miguel "Armillita" Espinosa stole the show.

Sanchez, 24, came to Mexico to confirm her status as a fully-fledged "matador" or bullfighter, a title granted last May. She was the first woman to don the traditional "suit of lights" in Mexico, although she toured Mexico last year while still a "novillera," or apprentice.
Many choice seats were unavailable at the box offices and were sold by ticket scalpers at up to 10 times their list price, at 2,000 pesos ($255).

The crowd of about 45,000 at the world's largest bullring made Sanchez visibly nervous. The crowd groaned in disappointment as a leg wound sustained during a practice session on Friday hampered Sanchez and casued her to fall as she faced her first bull.
"She was nervous and jumping around all over the place, she never settled down to dominate the bull," said economist Rosa Maria Chavez, an "aficionada".
To make up for the fans' disappointment, Espinosa paid to add a seventh bull to the day's programme which the 38-year-old managed to dispatch to a masterly death in the afternoon.
That finally drew shouts of "Ole" and the fans' white handkerchiefs, a traditional request that the fighter be awarded one of the bull's ears in tribute to a fine performance.
After her troubles with the first bull, Sanchez struggled again with her second, taking four attempts to kill the bull.
Opinions were generally charitable toward Sanchez and somewhat less so to the organisers.
"The bull was not up to scratch," said one fan.
"Thieves!" shouted other aficionados, annoyed at what they said were undersized and docile bulls not worthy of a prestigious bullring such as Mexico City.
